Computer Engineering
The Computer Engineering program equips students with the knowledge, skills, and hands-on experience needed to thrive in the dynamic field of computer engineering, fostering innovation and leadership in technology-driven industries.
Program Homepage
Program Handbook
The Computer Engineering program integrates advanced theory and practical applications to prepare students for leadership roles in the fields of computer hardware and software systems. This program emphasizes the intersection of hardware and software, providing students with a comprehensive understanding of computing technologies and their real-world applications.
Degrees Offered:
Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.)
Master of Engineering (M.Engr.)
Master of Science (M.S.)
Online Master of Engineering (M.Engr.)
Online Master of Science (M.S.)
Area(s) of Specialization: (may appear on ISU transcripts after graduation)
Computing and Networking Systems (M.S., Ph.D.)
Predictive Plant Phenomics (Ph.D.)
Secure and Reliable Computing (M.S., Ph.D.)
Software Systems (M.S., Ph.D.)
Very Large Scale Integration (M.S., Ph.D.)
Area(s) of Emphasis:
Information Systems Security/Networking
Software Systems
VLSI Design
How long does it take to earn a degree?
Median time to earn the doctorate: 5.2 years (Methods)
Median time to earn the master’s: 1.8 years (Methods)

Learning Goals
Demonstrate mastery of knowledge and scholarly literature in their fields of study.
Understand ethical principles and conduct responsible research
Effectively communicate and disseminate their technical contributions.
Students pursuing theses/dissertations shall also demonstrate ability to conduct state-of-the-art research and expand the knowledge base in their fields of study
Admission Requirements
Graduate College Requirements:
4 year Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent)
Academic Records/Transcripts
Minimum 3.0 GPA (Program may alter requirement.)
Proof of English Proficiency.
Program Specific Requirements:
GRE is optional
Three letters of recommendation are required to be submitted electronically with your online application.
The Master of Engineering is a course-based program primarily for online students. For additional information on the Master of Engineering program, click here.
The International Collaborative Education Program is intended for participating institutions that have an agreement with the College of Engineering. For additional information about the ICEP, please click here.

Application Deadlines:
For Fall entry, the funding priority deadline is January 15; for Spring entry, it is September 1. Applications are welcome after these dates, and will receive consideration for remaining admission and funding opportunities.
